designs.name: Haeckel Blue Jellyfish
designs.title: Jellyfish T Shirt Vintage Scientific Illustration Tee, Ernst Haeckel Blue Jellyfish Ocean Art, Unisex Cotton Marine Biology Gift
designs.design_paragraph: A jellyfish drawn in 1904 by Ernst Haeckel, the biologist who spent his life arguing that nature was already art before anyone drew it. This one is Cyanea annasethe — he named the species after his wife, Anna Sethe, who died the year before he first saw it. The trailing filaments are why.

designs.name: Haeckel Compass Jellyfish
designs.title: Compass Jellyfish T Shirt, Vintage Ernst Haeckel Illustration Tee, Gold Sea Life Art, Unisex Heavy Cotton Naturalist Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: The compass jellyfish, Chrysaora hysoscella, drawn by Ernst Haeckel in 1904 for Kunstformen der Natur — a book made to prove that a jellyfish is better designed than most things people design on purpose. Amber bell, tentacles going their own way.

designs.name: Orchid Skull
designs.title: Botanical Skull T Shirt, Vintage Anatomy Orchid Tee, Skeleton and Flowers Art, Unisex Heavy Cotton Goth Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: An anatomical skull from a sixteenth-century dissection atlas, with orchids growing out through the cranium. Two plates three hundred years apart, cut out and set in one ink so they read as one drawing rather than two scans.

designs.name: Overgrown Prison
designs.title: Overgrown Ruins T Shirt, Piranesi Etching Tee, Gothic Architecture Print, Vintage Engraving Unisex Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: One of Piranesi's imaginary prisons — staircases that go nowhere, arches holding up nothing — with two centuries of climbing growth let into it. He drew the impossible architecture in 1750; the plants came from a botanical plate and were never meant to be there.

designs.name: Moonlit Ghost
designs.title: Moon Ghost T Shirt, Japanese Yokai Woodblock Tee, Yoshitoshi Print Art, Vintage Star Chart Unisex Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: A figure from Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, set against a seventeenth-century star atlas. He was the last great woodblock artist and worked while the form was dying; the constellations behind are from Cellarius, who mapped a sky nobody had photographed yet.

designs.name: Marigold Calavera
designs.title: Calavera T Shirt, Day of the Dead Marigold Tee, Posada Skeleton Folk Art, Dia de los Muertos Unisex Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: A calavera by Jose Guadalupe Posada, who drew skeletons doing ordinary things for Mexico City broadsides and died broke in 1913. Wreathed here in marigolds — cempasuchil, the flower whose smell is supposed to guide the dead home.
designs.seasonal_note: Dia de Muertos is Nov 1-2 — must be ranking before it, not launching into it

designs.name: Metamorphosis
designs.title: Moth Metamorphosis T Shirt, Vintage Entomology Tee, Maria Merian Insect Plate Art, Unisex Heavy Cotton Nature Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: Caterpillar, chrysalis and moth on the plant that feeds them, drawn by Maria Sibylla Merian around 1700. She was the first person to draw insects with their host plants instead of pinned on blank paper, which is why the whole life cycle sits in one frame.

designs.name: Dore's Descent
designs.title: Fallen Angel T Shirt, Gustave Dore Engraving Tee, Gothic Illustration Print, Vintage Literature Unisex Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: Gustave Dore engraved for Dante and Milton in the 1860s and drew falling bodies better than anyone before or since. This one keeps his line and lets a botanical plate grow through the composition, which is not something he would have allowed.

designs.name: Fungi Codex
designs.title: Mushroom Chart T Shirt, Vintage Fungi Identification Tee, Cottagecore Forest Art, Mycology Unisex Heavy Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: Mushrooms from a nineteenth-century identification plate, laid out as a specimen grid the way the original charts did it — labelled, ordered, and drawn by someone who needed you to tell the edible one from the one that kills you.

designs.name: Kraken Chart
designs.title: Kraken T Shirt, Vintage Octopus Nautical Chart Tee, Sea Monster Map Art, Antique Maritime Unisex Cotton Gift Shirt
designs.design_paragraph: The colossal octopus Pierre Denys de Montfort drew in 1801 from sailors' accounts he mostly believed, pulling down a ship. Set over an antique chart of water nobody had properly surveyed. He was wrong about the size and right that something was down there.
